title: A block of changes that an AI proposes for the content of one game (ride-changes/1)
description: What a person pastes into the panel after talking to an AI. The server expands the selectors, does the arithmetic and checks every number against the schemas of the content; the block says what to change, not what the new numbers are.

game.description: The slug of the game the block is for, as the instruction names it. A block for another game is refused.

base.description: What the instruction was made from: the number of the pack that is live, the snapshot of the content and the code of the instruction. Copy all three from the BASE line of the data.

brief.description: The code of the instruction this block answers.

summary.description: One sentence, in the language of the person, saying what the block does.

ops.description: The operations, applied in this order to a working copy of the content.

slug.description: The name of a car or a part: lower case words joined by dashes.

id.description: A name for the operation, so that an error can point at it.

pointer.description: Where the number is in the document: a JSON pointer (RFC 6901) with no escapes. In a scale of the rules a * stands for exactly one name (a track, a rung, a product).

unit.description: What the value is counted in, as the instruction says for that number. It must be the unit of the number; this is how a mistake between a percent and a millionth is caught.

target.description: One document: a document of the rules, or one car or part.

condition.description: A value the field must equal, or a test: one of in, gte, lte, gt, lt.

select.description: Every car or part of a kind that has the fields it asks for: the server turns it into the list of those and shows the list.

where.description: Field => condition, every one of them true. A field is a name at the top of the document (slot, tier) or a name inside an object (engine/layout).

text.description: Sets the text of ONE language in a text that has several (a name, a description). The other languages stay as they are. No markup and no links.

path.description: The place of the text that has the languages, for example /name.

create.description: Makes a new car or part as a draft. `from` is the slug of one that exists: the new one starts as a copy of it (without its picture) and `fields` replaces whole fields of it. A new car or part cannot be changed by another operation of the same block: give its values in `fields`. Never give a picture.

slug.description: The slug of the new one: it is for good and is never used again.

fields.description: The fields of the car or part to set, as the tables of the data show them in the file (prices in cents, powers in the units of the file), a text as an object with its languages (give en, pl, fr, de and pt-BR).

set.description: Sets one number to a value.

value.description: The number in the unit of the number, as the instruction shows it (a percent as 12.5, dollars as 21500).

scale.description: Changes numbers by a percent of what they are now, in one go: +12 makes a number 12% greater, -5 makes it 5% less. The server does the arithmetic and the rounding.
